transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I’m a little embarrassed to say it, doctor. I’ve been having these nights where I eat more than I mean to, and afterward I’m just sitting there with crumbs and empty containers around me. I feel so ashamed and disgusted with myself… it gets so bad I can hardly pray, or look people at church in the eye the next morning. I don’t know if that’s the sort of thing you help with, but I thought I should come in.
Do you do anything to try to undo or make up for the amount you ate during these episodes?
Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I feel awful afterward, and I might tell myself I’ll “do better” the next day, but I don’t really have anything I do to undo it. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after one of these eating episodes?
No… no, I don’t make myself vomit. I’ve felt sick and ashamed after, but I don’t do that. Is that… is that what you were asking?
How often do these episodes of eating more than you mean to happen?

I suppose… more than I’d like to admit. Since my friend passed, it’s been happening at least once or twice most weeks, usually late at night. I keep hoping it’s just a rough patch, but I don’t think there’s been a whole month where it really stopped or let up.
Do you feel guilty or self-critical after these episodes of eating more than you meant to?

Yes… I do. I try not to be too hard on myself, but after those nights I’ll just sit there with the crumbs and empty containers around me and feel so ashamed. Disgusted with myself, really. Sometimes the next morning I can hardly pray, or look people at church in the eye. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but… yes, I do feel very guilty afterward.
During these episodes of eating more than you mean to, do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control how much you're eating?

Yes… I think so. I don’t like saying it that way, because I know it sounds awful, but once I take that first bite after the house is quiet, it’s like my good sense just sort of steps aside. I’ll even be telling myself, “Belinda, stop now,” and then my hands just keep reaching for more. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like you're eating much more quickly than usual during these episodes?

Yes… I think I do. I mean, not very ladylike to admit, but I’ll be standing there at the kitchen counter and eating so fast I hardly even taste the pound cake or the crackers. Sometimes I realize I’ve swallowed before I’ve really chewed properly. That’s… that’s not good, is it?
Do you feel like you have no control over what or how much you're eating during these episodes?

Yes… I suppose that is the right way to put it. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m helpless, but once I take that first bite after the house is quiet, it’s like my good sense just… steps aside. I’ll be saying to myself, “Belinda, stop now,” and still my hands keep reaching for more. So yes, I guess I don’t feel in control then.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since these episodes of eating more than you mean to started?

I’m… not really sure, doctor. I don’t weigh myself as much as I probably should, and I try not to look too closely, if I’m honest. My clothes may feel a little different now and then, but I couldn’t say it’s been a significant change. Is that okay to say?
Do you usually eat during these episodes when you're alone, or are there other people around?

Mostly alone, yes. I mean, when I’m at bridge or a church supper, I’ll take a sensible little plate like everyone else, nothing that would draw attention. But then later, after folks have gone home, I’ll sometimes go back to the kitchen and pull out the leftovers… and eat where nobody can see me. I’m embarrassed to say that, but that’s usually how it happens.
Do these episodes of eating more than you mean to interfere with your daily life or relationships in any way?

Well… I wouldn’t want to say it’s ruining anything, exactly. I still try to keep up appearances and do what I’m supposed to do. But I have started saying no to some bridge nights, and even to helping in the church kitchen, which I used to do more.

I suppose it’s because I worry someone will notice food missing, or… ask me why I’m acting so ashamed about leftovers and things. That sounds silly when I say it out loud, doesn’t it? But yes, it has made me pull back some.
Have these episodes of eating more than you mean to been happening for more than 3 months?

Yes… I suppose it has been more than three months. I hadn’t really counted it that way, but it’s been about five months now, since my closest bridge partner—my church friend—passed away. That’s when it seemed to start happening more.
Do you usually feel uncomfortably full after these episodes of eating more than you mean to?

Yes… I do, usually. I try to tell myself I’ll stop before it gets to that point, but I don’t always. I keep going until my stomach feels tight and sore, right under my nightgown, and then I have to sort of ease myself into the recliner because moving around hurts. It sounds awful to say it that plainly, but… yes, that happens.
Do you feel marked distress, such as depression or anxiety, after these episodes of eating more than you mean to?

Yes… I think that’s really why I came in, if I’m being honest. After those nights, I’ll be sitting there with crumbs and empty containers around me, and I just feel so ashamed. Disgusted with myself, really.

I don’t like saying it that strongly… but the next morning I can hardly pray properly, and I feel like I can’t look folks at church in the eye. It weighs on me quite a bit.
How many times a week do these episodes of eating more than you mean to usually happen?

Well… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but since my friend passed, it’s been at least once or twice most weeks. I don’t think there’s been a whole month where it really eased up or stopped.
